MINUTES
  MALIBU CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING
  FEBRUARY 12, 2024
  COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  6:30 P.M.

MEETING CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Uhring called the meeting to order at 6:36 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Mayor Steve Uhring; Mayor Pro Tem Doug Stewart; and Councilmembers
  Paul Grisanti, Marianne Riggins, and Bruce Silverstein

  ALSO PRESENT: Trevor Rusin, Interim City Attorney; Steve McClary, City Manager;
  Joseph Toney, Assistant City Manager; Alexis Brown, Deputy City Manager; Kelsey
  Pettijohn, City Clerk; Kristin Riesgo, Community Services Director; Yolanda Bundy,
  Environmental Sustainability Director Richard Mollica Planning Director Susan Duenas
  Pub11c Safety D1rector Parker Dav1s Medla Techn1c1an Christina Munoz Deputy C1ty
  Clerk Trav1s Hart and Deputy Pub11c Works Director

PLEE
  DG OF ALLEGIANCE

  Lester Tobias led the Pledge of Allegiance.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  City Clerk Pettijohn reported that the agenda for the meeting was properly posted on
  February 2, 2024, with the amended agenda posted on February 9, 2024.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Councilmember Grisanti moved, and Councilmember Silverstein seconded a
  motion to approve the agenda.

FRIENDLY AMENDMENT
  Councilmember Riggins moved to adjourn in memory of Matt Rapf.

  The amendment was accepted by the maker and the seconder of the motion.

  The motion carried unanimously.

ITEM 1  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS

  None.

ITEM 2.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  Lester Tobias discussed delayed planning approvals for his projects. He stated the
  additional contract planners did not improve the department’s response time.

  Fireball Lawrence announced 2] Miles in Malibu had won nine film festival
  awards. He announced a screening with Supervisor Horvath and Malibu High
  School.

  Jill Hawkins was not present at the time of the hearing.

  Jaime Francis stated he was unaware of the closed session regarding potential
  litigation over the housing element. He discussed the importance of the housing
  element‘and the City’s obligation to provide affordable housing.

  Ryan Embree stated the Planning Commission only had four members at its last
  meeting to consider an application to restore a wetland buffer at 23855 Civic Center
  Way. He expressed concern that the project would minimize the wetlands.

  Mario Sandoval, Mountains Recreation and Conservation Authority (MRCA)
  Coastal Planner, read a letter from Elena Eger into the record.

ITEM 2.B.  COMMISSION / COMMITTEE / CITY MANAGER UPDATES

  Fireball Lawrence, Malibu Arts Commission, stated Poet Laureate Nathan Hassall
  had lead poetry workshops for children and adults since assuming office in
  September 2023 and announced the next Caffeinated Verse event on February l7,
  2024. He announced The Ripple Effect: A Generative Poetry Workshop on
  February 24, 2024. He stated workshops had also been organized at all the Malibu
  schools. He stated the Malibu student art exhibit had opened on Monday and would
  close on March 10, 2024. He stated the next art exhibit would open on-March 24,
  2024 and feature art by Leigh McCloskey. He stated the Commission planned to
  continue the Art Talks program and had a program planned with Pep Williams.

  City Manager McClary discussed the storm last week and reported that the City did
  not have any significant issues, but the City was monitoring 34 parcels that showed
  signs of slope failure or coastal erosion. He stated CHP was actively patrolling
  PCH and provided statistics from the CHP Task Force for January 29-February 11,
  2024. He stated 154 citations were issued, 15 1 of those were for speeding, and ten
  verbal warnings were given. He stated an individual speeding over 100 mph was
  stopped and arrested for driving under the influence. He stated on February 8, 2024
  additional CHP officers were deployed in Malibu for targeted enforcement and
  resulted in 23 citations for moving Violations and 16 non—moving violations. He
  stated the City participated in the homeless count on January 24, 2024 and the local
  count showed 51 individuals experiencing homelessness in Malibu, the lowest
  count since 2016. He announced the new minimum wage effective July 1, 2024
  was $17.27 per hour. He announced the Agents of Discovery program for children
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of February 12, 2024
  Page 3 of 12

  aged 4-12, launching at Legacy Park. He stated he attended the Library
  Subcommittee meeting and a Business Roundtable meeting. He stated he attended
  the League of California Cities City Manager conference with Assistant City
  Manager Toney and Deputy City Manager Brown.

  Sergeant Chris Soderlund, Los Angeles County Sheriff” s Department, discussed the
  recent rainstorms and reported there were no significant issues. He discussed the
  earthquake on February 9, 2024, and the epicenter off Decker Road. He discussed
  the Sheriff Department’s critical facility checks in response to the earthquake and
  stated there was no damage to report He stated CHP had begun patrolllng PCH 1n
  Mallbu seven days a week He dlscussed an 1nc1dent where a suspect fled 1n
  response to a DEA search warrant and the Sheriff Department as31sted w1th
  apprehendlng the suspects He stated the afternoon crime suppress1on car had been
  investigating‘vehicle burglaries and they had identifled two vehicles associated
  with the burglaries and led to the arrest of a suspect. He reported crime statistics
  for January 2024. He stated there were 35 part one crimes, compared to 44 in 2023.
  He stated there were two residential burglaries in the Malibu West area. He stated
  he planned to meet with Malibu West HOA on February 21, 2024 to discuss
  burglaries and security.

B  In response to Councilmember Riggins, City Manager McClary stated staff would

  Councilmember Grisanti stated he read a new rule from the Department of
  Transportation outlining the types of studies for any work on PCH and other
  highways He stated this rule could support the City s effort to lower speed limits
  on PCH He announced a Los Angeles County Coastal ReSIhency Study meeting
  on February 28 2024 He d1scussed the draft State of Callforma Sea Level r1se
  guidance He dlscussed the Topanga Beach Lagoon Restoratlon prOJect and
  announced a meeting at the end of February. He stated he attended the SM-MUSD
  California Voting Rights Act (CVRA) hearings in Malibu and Santa Monica. He
  stated school district separation was still progressing. He recommended students
  apply for the Harry Barovsky Memorial Youth Commission and discussed the
  positive impact it had on its members.

  Councilmember Riggins stated she attended a Clean Power Alliance Board meeting
  and a Library Subcommittee meeting. She stated she attended the SM-MUSD
  CVRA hearing in Malibu and virtually attended the Santa Monica hearlng She
  announced the Pornt Dume Headlands weed pulling event on February 14 2024
  She announced the next Llbrary Speaker Serles event on February 21 2024 an
  organrcs recycllng trarmng on February 14 2024 and an e waste recycling event
  on February 17, 2024.

  Councilmember Silverstein thanked the public speakers and those who sent written

.comments. He discussed the challenges of bureaucracy and concerns he heard from
 the public that the system was not fair to everyone. He encouraged members ofthe
 public to share any concerns they have with the Councilmembers. He stated the
 City had held an open public hearing on the housing element and the closed session
 today was publicly noticed on an agenda. He recommended Mr. Francis look into
 the facts of the law. He stated a project on the Smith Parcel wetlands had been
 approved by the Planning Commission and he hoped the project would be brought
 before the Council. He discussed the Council’s ability to appeal decisions of
Planning Commission decisions and the 10-day window for the appeal. He stated
he would like to review the letters from the MRCA and California Coastal
 Commission. He stated he attended an Administration andFinance Subcommittee
meeting and a Library Subcommittee meeting. He discussed the latest homeless
count and stated one of his campaign platforms was to reduce the number ofpeople
experiencing homelessness in the City for the public’s safety. He stated the number
of people experiencing homelessness in the City had consistently decreased since
the election. He discussed his work on the No Camping ordinance to address the
issues with homelessness. He stated the No Camping ordinance could be more
strictly enforced, particularly to address individuals living in their car who had the
ability to travel to shelter. He stated he had received emails from individuals
seeking to appeal the Council's decision regarding the award of the half marathon
road race agreement. He stated that he understood the Council’s decision could not
be appealed, but he had reviewed all the comments.

Mayor Pro Tem Stewart stated he attended an Administration and Finance
Subcommittee meeting, and the SM—MUSD CVRA hearing in Malibu. He stated
he met with Senator Irwin’s staff and city staff to discuss PCH safety. He
commended the Public Works and Public Safety staff for their response to the
winter storm. He discussed the earthquake on February 9, 2024 and the importance
of earthquake preparedness. He stated the City had purchased automatic license
plate readers and they could have assisted in locating the burglary suspect with the
stolen plates if they were in operation. He discussed the Baker Tilly report and the
importance of getting an update on the implementation of those recommendations.
He discussed a Department of Transportation study and stated he looked forward
to reading it. He indicated agreement with Councilmember Silverstein’s comments
on the housing element. He stated the City was trying to comply with the law and
explained that work on the housing element was one of the things taking resources
away from other projects. He discussed homelessness and the communities’
support fOr individuals experiencing homelessness. He stated it was important to
help each person individually and explained that they each had different needs and
challenges.

Mayor Uhring stated Lindsay Horvath contacted him immediately after the
earthquake and rain‘ events to check on conditions in Malibu. He commended
Public Wgrks Director DuBoux, Public Safety Director Dueflas, and Environmental
Sustainability Director Bundy on their work in response to storms and earthquakes.
He announced an event at Adamson House at the end of February to tour the
Adamson House and Surfrider Beach. He stated he met with Assemblymember
   Malibu City Council

  Page 5 of 12

  Irwin and Mayor Pro Tem Stewart and she was optimistic about the proposed bill
  to allow speed cameras in Malibu. He stated the CVRA hearing Videos are
  available online. He stated he attended an event in Agoura Hills about the 101
  Freeway wildlife crossing. He stated he met with Captain Seetoo, Public Safety
  Director Duenas, and City Manager McClary to discuss potential measures to
  improve safety on PCH. He stated Captain Seetoo had put reserve Deputies in the
  fleld and had directed the crime suppression cars to patrol PCH when they were not
  responding to a call or writing reports in the field.
